verdict.line: You lose if you let Irelia stack Ionian Fervor and chip you with free Bladesurge resets; you win the moment you land Q (Obliterate) through her E (Flawless Duet) window and drag her into a Death's Grasp E.

brief.thesis: Irelia has the lane advantage because her Q (Bladesurge) and E (Flawless Duet) let her poke and disengage safely while Mordekaiser has no dash, but the 51.9% head-to-head over 1436 games says Mordekaiser wins the war of attrition once he lands Death's Grasp (E) and forces the all-in she can't escape. This is a lane about surviving her poke phase with W (Indestructible) shield banking, not winning early trades outright.

theirWindow.what: She can reset Q off a low-HP minion to chain another dash-strike at you for free poke; expect a Q-auto-Q pattern whenever a caster minion is about to die near you, since killing it refreshes her Q cooldown entirely.

yourWindow.when: She has no Q and E (Flawless Duet) on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Without Bladesurge up she has zero escape, so this is when you walk up and land E (Death's Grasp) to pull her into melee range and trade Q (Obliterate) freely; her 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s E cooldown is your green light.

powerCurve.note: Q resets and heal outpoke your no-mobility kit
Ionian Fervor stacking plus E stun punishes short trades
W shield banking lets you match her sustain
R (Realm of Death) turns skirmishes into isolation duels
Rylai's/Riftmaker burst outscales her flat AD scaling

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: Measured as the top start at 51.6% over 1279 games and 69.4% pick rate; the extra sustain and mana help you throw Q (Obliterate) and E (Death's Grasp) repeatedly through her poke phase without running dry.

boots.why: 88% pick rate and 51.3% win rate; Irelia's damage is almost entirely basic-attack-reliant once Ionian Fervor stacks up, so the flat reduction directly counters her Q (Bladesurge) and empowered autos.

core.why: First item in the top two measured paths (50.7% and 60.8% win rate); the slow from Q (Obliterate) and E (Death's Grasp) blunts her Q (Bladesurge) dash-ins and keeps her stuck in your R (Realm of Death).
Second item in both top build paths; the omnivamp sustains you through her poke and the true damage ramp wins extended trades she can't escape once pulled.
Appears in the 60.8% (51 games) and 61.8% (34 games, with Bramble Vest) build paths; grievous wounds shuts down her Q (Bladesurge) self-heal, which is her primary sustain tool in lane.

situational.when: she is all-in heavy early and you need the anti-heal and armor before level 6
she builds tankier and you need the burn damage over flat health
the game goes long and you want the extra utility slot

runes.keystoneWhy: Measured as the primary page at 52.2% pick rate; sustained melee trades through her poke phase stack Conqueror's healing, which directly answers her Q (Bladesurge) self-heal in a straight fight.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 78.1% of games at 50.7% win rate; Ignite's sustained burn and healing reduction punishes her Q (Bladesurge) heal and secures kills after you land R (Realm of Death), since she has no Flash-dodge for the execute.

playing.title: Hold E for her dash-in
playing.detail: Don't throw E (Death's Grasp) on cooldown; wait until she commits Q (Bladesurge) into you so the pull lands guaranteed and you can immediately follow with Q (Obliterate) and autos while she's stuck.

playing.title: Bank W, don't panic-heal
playing.detail: W (Indestructible) stores damage dealt and taken before you consume it to heal; let the shield build through her poke instead of popping it early, since the heal scales with stored damage.

playing.title: Track her E cooldown for walk-up windows
playing.detail: Flawless Duet (E) is her only hard stun on a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown; when it's down, you can walk up and trade freely without fear of the stun-into-auto combo.

playing.title: Save R for isolation, not poke trades
playing.detail: Realm of Death (R) is 140/120/100/90/80s cooldown and drags her alone with you, stealing stats; use it only when you can follow with full Q+E combo, not to answer a single poke.

playing.title: Never fight near a dying minion
playing.detail: If a low-HP minion is near you both, back off; killing it with Q (Bladesurge) fully refreshes her dash and lets her poke-and-reset indefinitely.

playing.title: Buy Thornmail timing around her power spike
playing.detail: Rush Thornmail once she hits two items; the grievous wounds removes her Q (Bladesurge) sustain entirely, turning her all-ins into pure damage races you win with Riftmaker.

playing.title: Respect Ionian Fervor stacks before extended trades
playing.detail: Watch her passive stack counter; at max stacks she gains bonus on-hit damage, so disengage short trades before she caps out rather than fighting through her spell rotation.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner choices above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the tactical reasoning connecting them to specific cooldowns and windows is my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Purchase Bramble Vest first. Focus on dodging Irelia’s (E) when fighting her. Keep an eye out for her Conqueror and (P) stacks before fighting her.
